**Marin Čilić** (Croatian pronunciation: [[mâriːn tʃǐːlitɕ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-8) born 28 September 1988) is a Croatian professional [tennis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis "Tennis") player. He has been ranked as high as world No. 3 in men's singles by the [Association of Tennis Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Tennis_Professionals "Association of Tennis Professionals") (ATP), achieved in January 2018. Čilić has won 21 [ATP Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_Tour "ATP Tour")-level singles titles, including a [major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\)#Tournaments "Grand Slam \(tennis\)") at the [2014 US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2014 US Open – Men's singles"). He was also runner-up at the [2017 Wimbledon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2017 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles") and the [2018 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2018 Australian Open – Men's singles"), and won an [ATP Masters 1000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_Masters_1000_tournaments "ATP Masters 1000 tournaments") event at the [2016 Cincinnati Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Western_&_Southern_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2016 Western & Southern Open – Men's singles"). 
Playing for his country, Čilić was pivotal in the [Croatian team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_Davis_Cup_team "Croatia Davis Cup team")'s victory at the [2018 Davis Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Davis_Cup_World_Group "2018 Davis Cup World Group"), and won an Olympic silver medal in men's doubles at the [2020 Tokyo Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_doubles "Tennis at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's doubles") partnering [Ivan Dodig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Dodig "Ivan Dodig"). Alongside [Goran Ivanišević](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goran_Ivani%C5%A1evi%C4%87 "Goran Ivanišević") and [Iva Majoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iva_Majoli "Iva Majoli"), he is widely considered to be one of the greatest Croatian tennis players in history.
Čilić has reached the semifinal stage or better at all four majors,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-9) and the quarterfinal stage or better at all nine Masters tournaments.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-10) He is one of only six [active players with 20 or more titles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_Tour_records#Other_active_players "ATP Tour records").
## Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]
Marin Čilić was born in [Medjugorje](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medjugorje "Medjugorje"), [SR Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SR_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "SR Bosnia and Herzegovina"), a town in [Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzegovina "Herzegovina"), to [Bosnian Croat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croats_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Croats of Bosnia and Herzegovina") parents. He was raised as a [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-12) His father Zdenko Čilić was determined that his sons – Marin and older brothers Vinko and Goran – would have the opportunities he lacked in playing sports. When the first tennis courts in the town were built in 1991, Marin and his friends were among the first to play on them. At the recommendation of [Goran Ivanišević](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goran_Ivani%C5%A1evi%C4%87 "Goran Ivanišević"), in 2004, at the age of 15, Čilić moved to [Sanremo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanremo "Sanremo"), Italy, to work with Ivanišević's former coach, [Bob Brett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Brett "Bob Brett").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-13)

## Career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Career")]
### 2004–05: Junior circuit
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2004–05: Junior circuit")]
Čilić began playing on the junior [ITF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Tennis_Federation "International Tennis Federation") circuit in spring 2004. At the start he played on clay courts, winning the _La Vie Junior Cup Villach_ in singles and the Dutch Junior Open in doubles. He then qualified for the [2004 US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_US_Open_\(tennis\) "2004 US Open \(tennis\)"), where he lost in the second round to [Sam Querrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Querrey "Sam Querrey"). In 2005, he won the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_French_Open "2005 French Open") title in Boys' singles, beating [Andy Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Murray "Andy Murray") in the semifinal[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-17) and [Antal van der Duim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antal_van_der_Duim "Antal van der Duim") in the final.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-18) He finished 2005 ranked number two behind American [Donald Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Young_\(tennis\) "Donald Young \(tennis\)"). While on the junior circuit, he won six tournaments in singles and four in doubles with his Canadian partner, Greg Kates.
Before representing Croatia, he played for [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina") as a junior with partner Zachary Rosen.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-19)
### 2005–2007: ATP Tour
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2005–2007: ATP Tour")]
In 2004, Čilić played one [Futures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITF_Men's_Circuit "ITF Men's Circuit") event (Croatia F1), at which he reached the second round; he finished the year tied at No. 1463 on the [rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_rankings "ATP rankings") of the [ATP Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_Tour "ATP Tour"). He played seven Futures tournaments in 2005, winning one, the Croatia F3 event; two [Challenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_Challenger_Tour "ATP Challenger Tour") tournaments, in Zagreb and Geneva; and one [ATP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Tennis_Professionals "Association of Tennis Professionals") International Series tournament, the [Croatia Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_Open "Croatia Open"), where he lost in the opening round. He finished the year ranked No. 587.
In 2006, he played three Futures, winning the Croatia F1 and Croatia F2 events. He also played in nine Challengers, nine International Series events (reaching the semifinals at [Gstaad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Open_\(tennis\) "Swiss Open \(tennis\)")),[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-fox101-20) and two [Davis Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davis_Cup "Davis Cup") ties, against [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria_Davis_Cup_team "Austria Davis Cup team") and [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina_Davis_Cup_team "Argentina Davis Cup team"). By the end of the year, he was ranked No. 170.
In 2007, he won the first and second professional tournaments of his career: the Casablanca Challenger (in April) and the Rijeka Challenger (in May). In June, at the [Queen's Club Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Queen's_Club_Championships "2007 Queen's Club Championships"), he beat [Tim Henman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Henman "Tim Henman") in the first round after trailing 2–4 in the final set, and reached the quarterfinals, where he fell to [Andy Roddick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Roddick "Andy Roddick"). After that performance, he reached a new career-high ranking of No. 101 on 18 June 2007.
In the World Group playoffs in the first round of the [2007 Davis Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Davis_Cup "2007 Davis Cup"), Čilić beat [Benjamin Becker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Becker "Benjamin Becker") of Germany; however, Croatia went on to lose the tie, three matches to two.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-ndtv1-21)
### 2008: First ATP singles title
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2008: First ATP singles title")]
In 2008, Čilić reached the semifinals at the [Chennai Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Open "Chennai Open"), in both singles and doubles. In the singles, he was defeated by [Mikhail Youzhny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Youzhny "Mikhail Youzhny"), who went on to win the tournament. Čilić made it to the fourth round of the [2008 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Australian_Open "2008 Australian Open"), taking out two [seeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed_\(sports\) "Seed \(sports\)") on his way, including [2007 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Australian_Open "2007 Australian Open") finalist [Fernando González](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Gonz%C3%A1lez "Fernando González"). [James Blake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Blake_\(tennis\) "James Blake \(tennis\)") beat him in the fourth round. He had achieved his goal for the year of reaching the top 40. His fourth-round result at the Australian Open put him at no. 39 in the ATP rankings.
Čilić also made it to the fourth round of [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Championships,_Wimbledon "The Championships, Wimbledon"), beating [Jarkko Nieminen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarkko_Nieminen "Jarkko Nieminen") in five sets in the second round and knocking-out 14th seed [Paul-Henri Mathieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul-Henri_Mathieu "Paul-Henri Mathieu"). At the 2008 Olympics, he reached the second round of the men's singles, beating [Juan Mónaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_M%C3%B3naco "Juan Mónaco") before losing to Fernando González.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-SR-22) He lost in straight sets to [Arnaud Clément](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arnaud_Cl%C3%A9ment "Arnaud Clément"). At the [Canada Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_Masters "Canada Masters"), he defeated Andy Roddick in reaching the quarterfinal stage, giving his best performance in a Masters Series tournament to date. He lost in three sets to [Gilles Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilles_Simon "Gilles Simon") in the quarterfinals.
Čilić played the [Pilot Pen Tennis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pilot_Pen_Tennis "Pilot Pen Tennis") tournament in New Haven, Connecticut, where he won his first ATP title. He defeated [Viktor Troicki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Troicki "Viktor Troicki"), [Jürgen Melzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Melzer "Jürgen Melzer"), and [Igor Andreev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Andreev "Igor Andreev") in early rounds, then 2007 finalist [Mardy Fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mardy_Fish "Mardy Fish") in the final. Čilić, seeded for the first time at a [Grand Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\) "Grand Slam \(tennis\)") tournament, reached the third round of the US Open, but lost to [Novak Djokovic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novak_Djokovic "Novak Djokovic") in a match that lasted almost four hours. Čilić came back from a break down in each of the second, third, and fourth sets. In the first round, he had defeated [Julien Benneteau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julien_Benneteau "Julien Benneteau") in five sets in a match that lasted more than four hours, winning the deciding set.
### 2009: US Open quarterfinals
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2009: US Open quarterfinals")]
Čilić won his first title of 2009 and second career ATP title at the [Chennai Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Chennai_Open "2009 Chennai Open"), defeating first-time finalist [Somdev Devvarman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somdev_Devvarman "Somdev Devvarman").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-23)
He reached the fourth round of the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2009 Australian Open – Men's singles") after beating [David Ferrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ferrer "David Ferrer") in straight sets, equalling his 2008 record. In the fourth round, he was defeated by [Juan Martín del Potro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Mart%C3%ADn_del_Potro "Juan Martín del Potro") in four sets. Later in the year, Čilić won the [PBZ Zagreb Indoors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBZ_Zagreb_Indoors "PBZ Zagreb Indoors"), defeating compatriot [Mario Ančić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_An%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Mario Ančić") in the final. He helped his country defeat Chilean opponents in the Davis Cup first-round tie by winning the opening singles match and joining forces with Mario Ančić to win the doubles rubber.
Čilić reached a career best at the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2009 French Open – Men's singles") when he beat 18th seed [Radek Štěpánek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radek_%C5%A0t%C4%9Bp%C3%A1nek "Radek Štěpánek") in the third round in straight sets. After two competitive sets against the third-seeded Andy Murray, Čilić lost the match.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-atpworldtour1-24)

He reached the second round of the [Queen's Club Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_Club_Championships "Queen's Club Championships"), an [ATP World Tour 250 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_World_Tour_250_series "ATP World Tour 250 series") event, where he was defeated by [Nicolas Mahut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Mahut "Nicolas Mahut") of France. He beat [Alberto Martín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Mart%C3%ADn "Alberto Martín") to make it into the second round at Wimbledon and won a five-set match (spread over two days) against Sam Querrey. He played another five-set match in the third round against [Tommy Haas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Haas "Tommy Haas"). He recovered from two sets down, but lost 10–8 in the deciding set, having held a match point.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-atpworldtour1-24)
During the hard-court season, Čilić was defeated in back-to-back events in the first round. At [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legg_Mason_Tennis_Classic "Legg Mason Tennis Classic"), he was defeated in straight sets by [Somdev Devvarman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somdev_Devvarman "Somdev Devvarman"). He then failed to duplicate his quarterfinal appearance in [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_Masters "Canada Masters"), losing to [Mikhail Youzhny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikhail_Youzhny "Mikhail Youzhny"). In the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2009 US Open – Men's singles"), as the 16th seed, he reached the fourth round, after defeating [Ryan Sweeting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Sweeting "Ryan Sweeting"), [Jesse Levine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Levine "Jesse Levine"), and [Denis Istomin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Istomin "Denis Istomin"). He defeated Levine after being down two sets to love, coming back to win. He then scored the biggest upset of the 2009 US Open with a straight-sets victory over second-seeded [Andy Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Murray "Andy Murray") in the fourth round. Čilić outclassed Murray by saving all the break points he faced and took advantage of Murray's unforced errors. After the match, he said it was the biggest win of his career to date. However, in the quarterfinals, he lost to the eventual champion Juan Martín del Potro, despite leading by one set and an opening break in the second set.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-atpworldtour1-24)
Following his impressive US Open run, Čilić participated in the [China Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_China_Open_\(tennis\) "2009 China Open \(tennis\)") in Beijing as the eighth seed. He won his opening match against Russian [Igor Andreev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Andreev "Igor Andreev"), followed by a three-set victory over Frenchman Julien Benneteau. In the quarterfinals, he defeated fourth seed [Nikolay Davydenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolay_Davydenko "Nikolay Davydenko"), before stunning world No. 2 and top seed (in the tournament) [Rafael Nadal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Nadal "Rafael Nadal") in a straightforward win. In the final, Čilić went down to second seed Novak Djoković in straight sets.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-atpworldtour1-24)
He reached the fifth final of his career at the [Bank Austria Tennis Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Bank_Austria-TennisTrophy "2009 Bank Austria-TennisTrophy") as top seed; however, he lost. He received a wild card for the [Davidoff Swiss Indoors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Davidoff_Swiss_Indoors "2009 Davidoff Swiss Indoors"), where he finished in the quarterfinals, losing to Radek Štěpánek. His final tournament of the year was the [BNP Paribas Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_BNP_Paribas_Masters "2009 BNP Paribas Masters"). Entered as 12th seed, he came from a set down to defeat [Łukasz Kubot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%81ukasz_Kubot "Łukasz Kubot") in the second round, and then from a set down again to defeat seventh seed [Fernando Verdasco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Verdasco "Fernando Verdasco"), before coming to a halt in the quarterfinals against eventual finalist [Gaël Monfils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ga%C3%ABl_Monfils "Gaël Monfils").
### 2010: First major semifinal and top 10 debut
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2010: First major semifinal and top 10 debut")]
Čilić won the [Chennai Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Chennai_Open "2010 Chennai Open") final, beating [Stan Wawrinka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stan_Wawrinka "Stan Wawrinka") of Switzerland in straight sets.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-atpworldtour1-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-25)
Seeded 14th at the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2010 Australian Open – Men's singles"), he defeated [Fabrice Santoro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabrice_Santoro "Fabrice Santoro"), [Bernard Tomic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Tomic "Bernard Tomic"), and Stan Wawrinka in the first three rounds. In the fourth round, he faced fourth seed and reigning US Open champion del Potro; it was their third meeting in the past five majors. In a match that lasted more than four and a half hours, Čilić defeated Del Potro to reach his second major quarterfinal appearance. In the quarterfinals, he defeated seventh seed Andy Roddick in another five-set victory. In doing so, he became the first Croatian to reach the semifinals at the Australian Open. However, Čilić eventually lost in four sets to Andy Murray, despite winning the first set. Čilić followed up his Australian campaign by defending his title in Zagreb, defeating [Michael Berrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Berrer "Michael Berrer") in the final. Čilić achieved a new career-high ranking of No. 9 as a result. Čilić was selected to play singles and doubles partnering with Karlović for the [Croatia Davis Cup team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_Davis_Cup_team "Croatia Davis Cup team") against [Ecuador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuador_Davis_Cup_team "Ecuador Davis Cup team") in March 2010. Čilić, seeded eighth, lost in the second round to [Guillermo García-López](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillermo_Garc%C3%ADa-L%C3%B3pez "Guillermo García-López") at the [BNP Paribas Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_BNP_Paribas_Open "2010 BNP Paribas Open").
At the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2010 French Open – Men's singles"), Čilić lost to [Robin Söderling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_S%C3%B6derling "Robin Söderling") in the fourth round. Čilić was defeated in the first round of [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2010 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles") by [Florian Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florian_Mayer "Florian Mayer").
He reached the semifinals of the [Legg Mason Tennis Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legg_Mason_Tennis_Classic "Legg Mason Tennis Classic") in Washington D.C., ending [Mardy Fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mardy_Fish "Mardy Fish")'s 11-match winning-streak in the third round. Čilić was defeated by eventual champion David Nalbandian.
At the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2010 US Open – Men's singles"), Čilić lost to [Kei Nishikori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kei_Nishikori "Kei Nishikori") in the second round.
### 2011: Sixth ATP title
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2011: Sixth ATP title")]
Čilić began the season with a first-round loss to Kei Nishikori in [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Aircel_Chennai_Open "2011 Aircel Chennai Open"), failing to defend his title. At the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Australian_Open "2011 Australian Open") he progressed to the fourth round, defeating [Donald Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Young_\(tennis\) "Donald Young \(tennis\)"), [Santiago Giraldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Giraldo "Santiago Giraldo"), and then [John Isner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Isner "John Isner") in a five-set. In the fourth round, he lost to world No. 1, Rafael Nadal. Next, he went to [Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagreb_Open "Zagreb Open") to defend another title. Again, he was unable to do so, falling to Florian Mayer in the quarterfinals.
Čilić played next in [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_ABN_AMRO_World_Tennis_Tournament "2011 ABN AMRO World Tennis Tournament") and lost to [Viktor Troicki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Troicki "Viktor Troicki") in the quarterfinals. He then played in [Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Open_13 "2011 Open 13"), where he was unseeded. He defeated [Tomáš Berdych](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%C3%A1%C5%A1_Berdych "Tomáš Berdych") in the quarterfinals and saved one match point in a comeback win against Mikhail Youzhny. He lost to Robin Söderling in the final. Čilić played for Croatia in the World Group playoffs in the first round of the [2011 Davis Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Davis_Cup "2011 Davis Cup"), defeating Florian Mayer in the opening singles rubber. He levelled the tie at 2–2 by defeating [Philipp Kohlschreiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philipp_Kohlschreiber "Philipp Kohlschreiber") in the first reverse singles rubber. However, Germany ultimately won the tie.
Čilić lost in the first round of the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2011 French Open – Men's singles") to [Rubén Ramírez Hidalgo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Ram%C3%ADrez_Hidalgo "Rubén Ramírez Hidalgo") and at [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2011 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles") to his compatriot [Ivan Ljubičić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Ljubi%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Ivan Ljubičić").
At Umag, Čilić became the first Croatian man to reach the finals in over 20 years, losing to [Alexandr Dolgopolov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandr_Dolgopolov "Alexandr Dolgopolov"). He upset Juan Martín del Potro in the second round of the [Rogers Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Cup_\(tennis\) "Rogers Cup \(tennis\)") and reached the third round of the US Open, losing to Roger Federer. In ATP 500 in Beijing, he lost the final against world No. 6, [Tomáš Berdych](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%C3%A1%C5%A1_Berdych "Tomáš Berdych"), in three sets. The next week he was upset by [Albert Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Ramos "Albert Ramos") in the [Shanghai Rolex Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai_Rolex_Masters "Shanghai Rolex Masters"). He won his sixth career title in Saint Petersburg by defeating world No. 10 [Janko Tipsarević](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janko_Tipsarevi%C4%87 "Janko Tipsarević") in the final. En route to the final, he defeated [Sergei Bubka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergei_Bubka_\(tennis\) "Sergei Bubka \(tennis\)"), [Somdev Devvarman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somdev_Devvarman "Somdev Devvarman"), [Andreas Seppi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andreas_Seppi "Andreas Seppi"), and Mikhail Youzhny.
### 2012: Two ATP titles
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2012: Two ATP titles")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Flickr_-_Carine06_-_Marin_Cilic_%281%29.jpg/250px-Flickr_-_Carine06_-_Marin_Cilic_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flickr_-_Carine06_-_Marin_Cilic_\(1\).jpg)Čilić during the final of the [2012 Queen's Club Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Queen's_Club_Championships "2012 Queen's Club Championships")
Čilić did not play at the [2012 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Australian_Open "2012 Australian Open"), but did play at [Indian Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_BNP_Paribas_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2012 BNP Paribas Open – Men's singles"), where he lost in the second round to [David Nalbandian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nalbandian "David Nalbandian"). He was defeated by Juan Martín del Potro in the third round of [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Sony_Ericsson_Open "2012 Sony Ericsson Open") and the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2012 French Open – Men's singles"). In June, Čilić won the [Queen's Club Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_Club_Championships "Queen's Club Championships") in London after his opponent in the final, David Nalbandian, was disqualified in the second set for aggravated behaviour, having kicked the hoarding around a linesman's chair, injuring the linesman.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-26)
In the third round of Wimbledon, he beat [Sam Querrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Querrey "Sam Querrey") 7–6, 6–4, 6–7, 6–7, 17–15 in the second-longest match ever played at Wimbledon in 5 hours and 31 minutes.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-27) He subsequently lost to Andy Murray in the following round. In July 2012, Čilić became the first home player to win the [Croatia Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_Open "Croatia Open") after 22 years by defeating [Marcel Granollers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcel_Granollers "Marcel Granollers") of Spain in the final.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-atp101-28)
At the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics"), he reached the second round in the men's singles, beating Jürgen Melzer before losing to Lleyton Hewitt.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-SR-22) In the men's doubles, he reached the quarterfinals with [Ivan Dodig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Dodig "Ivan Dodig").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-SR-22)
Čilić was seeded 12th at the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_US_Open_\(tennis\) "2012 US Open \(tennis\)"), where he matched his 2009 effort in reaching the quarterfinals. He was defeated by the eventual champion Andy Murray despite winning the first set and leading 5–1 in the second set.
### 2013: Failed drugs test and ban
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2013: Failed drugs test and ban")]
Čilić started his year at the [Chennai Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai_Open "Chennai Open"), where he lost to [Benoît Paire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beno%C3%AEt_Paire "Benoît Paire") in the quarterfinals. At the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2013 Australian Open – Men's singles"), he was seeded 12th but was upset in the third round by Andreas Seppi in a five-set match. In February, Čilić played for Croatia in the [Davis Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Davis_Cup "2013 Davis Cup") World Group playoffs against Italy; he defeated [Paolo Lorenzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paolo_Lorenzi "Paolo Lorenzi") in the opening singles rubber, and in the first reverse singles, he avenged his earlier loss to Seppi at the Australian Open, prevailing in a straight-sets win. Italy, however, won the tie eventually with a final score of 3–2.
At [Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBZ_Zagreb_Indoors "PBZ Zagreb Indoors"), where he had won twice in 2009 and 2010, Čilić won for a third time to earn his ninth career title, defeating [Jürgen Melzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Melzer "Jürgen Melzer") in the final. Čilić was top-seeded in the [Memphis Indoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_U.S._National_Indoor_Tennis_Championships "2013 U.S. National Indoor Tennis Championships") event but lost to [Kei Nishikori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kei_Nishikori "Kei Nishikori"), the eventual champion, in the quarterfinals. Čilić next played at [Indian Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_BNP_Paribas_Open "2013 BNP Paribas Open"), where he lost in the third round to [Milos Raonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milos_Raonic "Milos Raonic") in three sets. In the following tournament at [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Open_Tennis "Sony Open Tennis"), he defeated world No. 8, [Jo-Wilfried Tsonga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo-Wilfried_Tsonga "Jo-Wilfried Tsonga"), in the fourth round but lost to Andy Murray in the quarterfinals.
Čilić started his clay-court season in [Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte-Carlo_Masters "Monte-Carlo Masters"), but lost to [Richard Gasquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Gasquet "Richard Gasquet") in the fourth round. In May, it was announced Čilić had left his longtime coach [Bob Brett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Brett "Bob Brett") and would be coachless at tournaments before hiring a new one.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-29) At the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2013 French Open – Men's singles"), he lost in the third round to Viktor Troicki in straight sets. In June, Čilić returned to [Queen's Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_Club_Championships "Queen's Club Championships") to defend his title. He defeated world No. 6, Tomas Berdych, in the quarterfinals, his second top 10 win of the year, and [Lleyton Hewitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lleyton_Hewitt "Lleyton Hewitt") in the semifinal. In the final, Čilić lost to Andy Murray in three sets.
At [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2013 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles") Čilić pulled out before his second-round match claiming he had a left knee injury where he was scheduled to play [Kenny de Schepper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_de_Schepper "Kenny de Schepper") of France.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-30) However, a month later it was revealed that Čilić had pulled out due to failing a drugs test in Munich for, according to [Jutarnji list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jutarnji_list "Jutarnji list") daily, "incautious use of glucose."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-31) On 16 September 2013, he received a backdated nine-month ban due to testing positive for the banned substance [nikethamide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikethamide "Nikethamide"). Čilić claimed that the banned substance was ingested via Coramine glucose tablets bought at a pharmacy by a member of his team, and as a result, the independent tribunal believed that he did not intend to enhance his performance. The suspension ran until 1 February 2014 and all prize money and points since the positive test including the Munich tournament were null and forfeited.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-32) Čilić appealed against this ban to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, who reduced the ban from nine months to four months on 25 October. They stated that "the degree of fault committed by the athlete was inferior to that established in the (tribunal) decision and the sanction imposed was too severe in view of the degree of fault". Čilić, whose ranking had dropped to number 47, received an immediate boost as results at the French Open, Queen's and Wimbledon were reinstated.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-34)
In late 2013, Čilić started working with [Goran Ivanišević](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goran_Ivani%C5%A1evi%C4%87 "Goran Ivanišević") as his new coach.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-35)
### 2014: US Open champion
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: 2014: US Open champion")]
Main article: [2014 Marin Čilić tennis season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87_tennis_season "2014 Marin Čilić tennis season")

In [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Apia_International_Sydney "2014 Apia International Sydney"), he lost to Denis Istomin in the second round. At the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Australian_Open "2014 Australian Open") second round, Čilić lost to [Gilles Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilles_Simon "Gilles Simon") in five sets.
In February, Čilić successfully defended his title at [Zagreb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_PBZ_Zagreb_Indoors "2014 PBZ Zagreb Indoors") without dropping a set, winning his 10th career title. He defeated [Lukas Rosol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lukas_Rosol "Lukas Rosol"), world No. 10, Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, world No. 6, Andy Murray and [Igor Sijsling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Sijsling "Igor Sijsling"), reaching the second final of the season, where he lost to Tomas Berdych. Čilić continued his excellent form in [Delray Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delray_Beach_International_Tennis_Championships "Delray Beach International Tennis Championships"), reaching his third consecutive final of the season, where he defeated [Kevin Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Anderson_\(tennis\) "Kevin Anderson \(tennis\)") and won his 11th singles title.

He lost in early rounds in both [Madrid Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Mutua_Madrid_Open "2014 Mutua Madrid Open") and [Rome Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Internazionali_BNL_d'Italia "2014 Internazionali BNL d'Italia").
