In the warmup [US Open Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Open_Series "US Open Series"), Čilić advanced to the third round at [Rogers Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Rogers_Cup_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2014 Rogers Cup – Men's singles"), where he lost to Roger Federer in a close three-set match. In the following [Cincinnati Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Western_&_Southern_Open "2014 Western & Southern Open"), Čilić also reached the third round before losing to Stan Wawrinka.
Seeded 14th at the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_US_Open_\(tennis\) "2014 US Open \(tennis\)"), Čilić defeated [Marcos Baghdatis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_Baghdatis "Marcos Baghdatis"), [Illya Marchenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illya_Marchenko "Illya Marchenko") and Kevin Anderson to set up a fourth-round fixture against Gilles Simon, beating the Frenchman for the first time in five matches. He then went on to defeat both world No. 7, Tomas Berdych, and world No. 3, Roger Federer, in straight sets to reach his maiden major final. This was also his first-ever victory against Federer in all competitions. Čilić defeated 10th seed Kei Nishikori in straight sets in the final, claiming his first major title and becoming the first Croatian to win a men's major title since his coach Goran Ivanišević won the [2001 Wimbledon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Wimbledon_Championships "2001 Wimbledon Championships").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-bbc1-36) His triumph in the final was also his 300th professional victory.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-37)
Following his US Open victory, Čilić played for Croatia in [Davis Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Davis_Cup "2014 Davis Cup") World Group playoffs against Netherlands. Initially signed up for doubles rubber only, Čilić and teammate [Marin Draganja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_Draganja "Marin Draganja") beat [Robin Haase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Haase "Robin Haase") and [Jean-Julien Rojer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Julien_Rojer "Jean-Julien Rojer"). After a 2:2 tie between two countries, however, Čilić stepped up and played the deciding fifth singles rubber in place of young compatriot [Borna Ćorić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borna_%C4%86ori%C4%87 "Borna Ćorić"), where he defeated [Thiemo de Bakker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiemo_de_Bakker "Thiemo de Bakker"). The victory earned Croatia the World Group status for 2015.
At [China Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_China_Open_\(tennis\) "2014 China Open \(tennis\)"), Čilić advanced to the quarterfinal before losing to Andy Murray. In [Shanghai Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Shanghai_Rolex_Masters "2014 Shanghai Rolex Masters"), Čilić was upset in the first round by fellow countryman [Ivo Karlović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivo_Karlovi%C4%87 "Ivo Karlović") after losing the tiebreak in the third set. Čilić, however, rebounded at [Kremlin Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Kremlin_Cup "2014 Kremlin Cup"), where he defeated [Roberto Bautista Agut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Bautista_Agut "Roberto Bautista Agut") in the final and won his fourth title of the season. On 18 October, it was announced Čilić, as the then reigning US Open champion, had become the fifth player (after Djokovic, Nadal, Federer and Wawrinka) to qualify for the [ATP World Tour Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_ATP_World_Tour_Finals "2014 ATP World Tour Finals") in London from 9–16 November.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-38) Čilić subsequently withdrew from the [Valencia Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Valencia_Open_500 "2014 Valencia Open 500") and [Paris Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_BNP_Paribas_Masters "2014 BNP Paribas Masters") in order to allow time for an arm injury to heal before the tour finals. He ultimately lost all three matches in the round robin.
Čilić finished the season as world No. 9 in year-end ATP rankings.
### 2015: Fourteenth ATP title
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: 2015: Fourteenth ATP title")]
A shoulder injury prevented Čilić from playing the [Brisbane International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane_International "Brisbane International") and [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Australian_Open "2015 Australian Open").
After being sidelined for more than two months, Čilić made his season debut at the [Indian Wells Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_BNP_Paribas_Open "2015 BNP Paribas Open"). After receiving a bye in the first round, he lost in the second round to Juan Mónaco in straight sets. Čilić subsequently withdrew from the [Miami Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Miami_Open "2015 Miami Open") due to the shoulder problem. Čilić returned to tour at [Monte-Carlo Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Monte-Carlo_Rolex_Masters "2015 Monte-Carlo Rolex Masters"), where he advanced to quarterfinals, before losing to eventual champion Novak Djokovic.
At the 2015 French Open, Čilić lost to David Ferrer in the fourth round in straight sets. At [Queen's Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_Club "Queen's Club"), Čilić was beaten in the second round by [Victor Troicki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Troicki "Victor Troicki") in three sets. Čilić matched his 2014 Wimbledon performance, reaching the quarterfinals again after eliminating [Moriya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiroki_Moriya "Hiroki Moriya"), [Berankis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ri%C4%8Dardas_Berankis "Ričardas Berankis"), [Isner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Isner "John Isner") (12–10 in the fifth set), and [Kudla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Kudla "Denis Kudla").
Čilić returned to Flushing Meadows for the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_US_Open_\(tennis\) "2015 US Open \(tennis\)") to defend his title, reaching the semi-finals where he was beaten in straight sets by [Novak Djokovic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novak_Djokovic "Novak Djokovic") who also went on to win in the final. Čilić managed to defend his title at the [Kremlin Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Kremlin_Cup "2015 Kremlin Cup"), winning the final in almost identical fashion to the previous year. In the final, he defeated the same player as the previous year, Roberto Bautista Agut.
### 2016: First Masters title and Davis Cup final
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2016: First Masters title and Davis Cup final")]
In the first major tournament of the year, Marin Čilić was seeded 12th, but he was upset by Bautista Agut in the third round of the Australian Open.
At Indian Wells, he reached the quarterfinals before losing to No. 15 seed David Goffin. At the Miami Masters, he was defeated by Gilles Simon in third round.
At the [Wimbledon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2016 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles"), Čilić repeated his efforts of the previous two years making the quarterfinals, after eliminating rival Kei Nishikori in the fourth round. In the quarterfinals, he met third seed Roger Federer; Čilić won the first two sets and had match points in the fourth set but was unable to convert eventually being eliminated in five sets.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-39)
At the [2016 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics"), he competed in the men's singles and the men's doubles with [Marin Draganja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_Draganja "Marin Draganja"). He reached the last 16 in the singles and the second round in the doubles.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-40)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-41)
In August 2016, Čilić announced his new coach as [Jonas Björkman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonas_Bj%C3%B6rkman "Jonas Björkman") in a video posted to MyATP. In [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Western_&_Southern_Open "2016 Western & Southern Open"), Čilić claimed his maiden Masters title, defeating Andy Murray in the final in straight sets. This win ended Murray's 22-match winning streak, dating back to 2016 Queen's Club. The Croat beat Viktor Troicki, Fernando Verdasco, Tomáš Berdych, [Borna Ćorić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borna_%C4%86ori%C4%87 "Borna Ćorić") and Grigor Dimitrov in the route to the final. Čilić returned to the top 10 in the following week.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-42)
In October, he captured his maiden ATP 500 level title at the [Swiss Indoors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Swiss_Indoors "2016 Swiss Indoors"), beating Nishikori in straight sets in the final. At the [Paris Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Paris_Masters "2016 Paris Masters"), Čilić defeated Djokovic for the first time in his career to reach the semifinals, where he subsequently lost to John Isner. His run guaranteed that he would qualify for the [ATP World Tour Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_World_Tour_Finals "ATP World Tour Finals") for the second time in three years. There, in the round robin, he lost to Murray and Wawrinka, but defeated Nishikori for his first-ever win at the Finals. With this victory, he rose to No. 6 in the ATP rankings.
In the final of the [Davis Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Davis_Cup_World_Group "2016 Davis Cup World Group"), with Croatia leading Argentina by 2–1 in matches, Čilić led [Juan Martín del Potro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Mart%C3%ADn_del_Potro "Juan Martín del Potro") by two sets to love needing one more set to win the title for his country. However, del Potro went on to win the match in five sets and Argentina won the deciding match to win the tournament.
### 2017: Wimbledon final
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: 2017: Wimbledon final")]
Čilić started his 2017 season as first seed at the [Chennai Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Aircel_Chennai_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2017 Aircel Chennai Open – Singles") but lost to [Jozef Kovalík](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jozef_Koval%C3%ADk "Jozef Kovalík") in the second round. In the first major of the year, the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Australian_Open "2017 Australian Open"), Čilić lost in the second round to [Dan Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Evans_\(tennis\) "Dan Evans \(tennis\)").
In February, he lost in his opening match in [Montpellier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Open_Sud_de_France_%E2%80%93_Singles "2017 Open Sud de France – Singles"), reached the quarterfinals of the [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_ABN_AMRO_World_Tennis_Tournament_%E2%80%93_Singles "2017 ABN AMRO World Tennis Tournament – Singles"), and the semifinals of [Acapulco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Abierto_Mexicano_Telcel_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2017 Abierto Mexicano Telcel – Men's singles").
Čilić was eliminated in the second rounds of [Indian Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_BNP_Paribas_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2017 BNP Paribas Open – Men's singles"), [Miami Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Miami_Open "2017 Miami Open"), and [Madrid Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Mutua_Madrid_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2017 Mutua Madrid Open – Men's singles"), but reached the quarterfinals in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Internazionali_BNL_d'Italia "2017 Internazionali BNL d'Italia"), and [Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Monte-Carlo_Rolex_Masters_%E2%80%93_Singles "2017 Monte-Carlo Rolex Masters – Singles"). In May, Čilić won the title at the [Istanbul Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Istanbul_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2017 Istanbul Open – Singles"), defeating Milos Raonic in the final, in straight sets. This was his 14th ATP 250 title, second clay title, and 17th title overall. Additionally, Čilić's victory in Istanbul meant that 2017 was his tenth consecutive year winning at least one ATP title.
Čilić reached the quarterfinal of the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2017 French Open – Men's singles") for the first time in his career and thus became one of the few tennis players who reached the quarterfinal stage of every major championship.
In June, at the Queen's Club Championships, Marin made the final for the third time in his career. There he faced [Feliciano López](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feliciano_L%C3%B3pez "Feliciano López"), losing in three sets, after having a championship point in the final-set tiebreaker. At [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Championships,_Wimbledon "The Championships, Wimbledon"), Čilić reached the quarterfinals without dropping a set. There, he defeated Gilles Müller in five sets to reach his first Wimbledon semifinal. In the semifinal he recovered from a one set deficit to defeat Sam Querrey in four sets. In the final he was defeated by Roger Federer in straight sets, struggling with blisters on his left foot.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-43)
An adductor injury forced Čilić to miss the Montreal and Cincinnati Masters events.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-44) Čilić returned to play at the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_US_Open_\(tennis\) "2017 US Open \(tennis\)") where he lost to [Diego Schwartzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Schwartzman "Diego Schwartzman") in the third round.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-45) Despite this, following the tournament's conclusion Čilić broke into the top five for the first time in his career.
In October, Čilić reached the semifinals of the [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Rakuten_Japan_Open_Tennis_Championships_%E2%80%93_Singles "2017 Rakuten Japan Open Tennis Championships – Singles"), [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Shanghai_Rolex_Masters_%E2%80%93_Singles "2017 Shanghai Rolex Masters – Singles"), [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Swiss_Indoors_%E2%80%93_Singles "2017 Swiss Indoors – Singles"), and the quarterfinals of the [Paris Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Rolex_Paris_Masters_%E2%80%93_Singles "2017 Rolex Paris Masters – Singles"). Čilić failed to win a match in the [ATP Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_ATP_Finals "2017 ATP Finals") despite going to three sets against Federer, [Alexander Zverev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Zverev "Alexander Zverev"), and [Jack Sock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Sock "Jack Sock"). Čilić finished the season as world No. 6 for the second consecutive year.
### 2018: Australian final, Davis Cup champion, world No. 3
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: 2018: Australian final, Davis Cup champion, world No. 3")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/Cilic_WM18_%2862%29_%2843932286881%29.jpg/250px-Cilic_WM18_%2862%29_%2843932286881%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cilic_WM18_\(62\)_\(43932286881\).jpg)Čilić at the [2018 Wimbledon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Wimbledon_Championships "2018 Wimbledon Championships")
Čilić started his 2018 season as first seed in [Pune, India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Maharashtra_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2018 Maharashtra Open – Singles"). He lost in semifinals to eventual champion Gilles Simon.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-46)
Despite mixed form since his Wimbledon campaign, Čilić defeated world No. 1, [Rafael Nadal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Nadal "Rafael Nadal"), at the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Australian_Open "2018 Australian Open") after the Spaniard retired hurt in the fifth set, going on to reach another Grand-Slam final against Federer. This made him the first Croatian to ever reach the singles final at Melbourne Park. He eventually lost in five sets. The match garnered minor criticism from some tennis pundits for being played indoors to favour Federer, despite the Australian Open traditionally being an outdoor event. Čilić later admitted that he found it difficult to adjust to the changed conditions. However, it remained disputed that who among the two players was going to be favored in indoor conditions.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-47) At the conclusion of the tournament, Čilić reached a career-high ATP ranking of No. 3. He remained at that position for 12 weeks, before being surpassed by [Alexander Zverev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Zverev_Jr. "Alexander Zverev Jr."). 
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87%2C_finale_Coupe_Davis_2018.jpg/330px-Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87%2C_finale_Coupe_Davis_2018.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87,_finale_Coupe_Davis_2018.jpg)Čilić after victory vs Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, [2018 Davis Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Davis_Cup "2018 Davis Cup"), final
In the first two [Masters 1000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masters_1000 "Masters 1000") events of the season Čilić was defeated by Philipp Kohlschreiber (at [Indian Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_BNP_Paribas_Open "2018 BNP Paribas Open"), in the round of 32) and John Isner, the eventual champion of [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Miami_Open "2018 Miami Open"). In the clay-court season, Čilić played four tournaments reaching the quarterfinals of [Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Monte-Carlo_Masters "2018 Monte-Carlo Masters"), the semifinals of [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Italian_Open "2018 Italian Open"), and the quarterfinals at the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_French_Open "2018 French Open"). Čilić failed to defend his only title from the 2017 season at [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Istanbul_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2018 Istanbul Open – Singles"), losing in his opening match to [Malek Jaziri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malek_Jaziri "Malek Jaziri"). This defeat marked the first time since February 2014 that Čilić had not held any tournament on the ATP Tour.
At [Queen's Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Queen's_Club_Championships_%E2%80%93_Singles "2018 Queen's Club Championships – Singles"), Čilić was the top seed. He reached the final, where he contested a close match with Djokovic, coming out on top in three sets and saving a match point on his serve to claim his second title at Queen's Club and second career win over Djokovic. At [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2018 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles"), he was drawn in the top half and was considered one of the biggest threats to Roger Federer's title defense. He was upset in the second round by [Guido Pella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guido_Pella "Guido Pella") in five sets, after comfortably winning the first two sets.
During the North American summer hard-court swing, Čilić made strong showings in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Rogers_Cup_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2018 Rogers Cup – Men's singles") and [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Western_&_Southern_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2018 Western & Southern Open – Men's singles"), losing in both tournaments to the eventual champion in tight three setters (Rafael Nadal in Toronto and Novak Djokovic in Cincinnati). At the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2018 US Open – Men's singles"), Čilić recovered from a two-set deficit to defeat teenager [Alex de Minaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_de_Minaur "Alex de Minaur") in the third round. Čilić eventually lost in the quarterfinals against Kei Nishikori in a rematch of the [2014 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2014 US Open – Men's singles").
Čilić helped Croatia reach the [Davis Cup finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Davis_Cup_World_Group "2018 Davis Cup World Group") for the second time in three years, winning one of his two singles rubbers against the [USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Davis_Cup_team "United States Davis Cup team"). In October, Čilić suffered a string of early exits at [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Rakuten_Japan_Open_Tennis_Championships_%E2%80%93_Singles "2018 Rakuten Japan Open Tennis Championships – Singles"), [Shanghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Shanghai_Rolex_Masters_%E2%80%93_Singles "2018 Shanghai Rolex Masters – Singles"), and [Basel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Swiss_Indoors_%E2%80%93_Singles "2018 Swiss Indoors – Singles"). He rebounded from this trough in form at the [Paris Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Rolex_Paris_Masters_%E2%80%93_Singles "2018 Rolex Paris Masters – Singles") reaching the quarterfinals for a third consecutive year before losing to Djokovic in three sets. By winning a set he ended the Serb's streak of 30 consecutive sets won.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-48)
Čilić qualified for the [Tour Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_ATP_Finals_%E2%80%93_Singles "2018 ATP Finals – Singles") for a third successive time and fourth time overall. His disappointing record at the event continued winning only one of his three round-robin matches, bringing his overall record at the event to 2–10.
Čilić led the [Croatian national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_Davis_Cup_team "Croatia Davis Cup team") at the [2018 Davis Cup final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Davis_Cup_World_Group#France_vs._Croatia "2018 Davis Cup World Group") against [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_Davis_Cup_team "France Davis Cup team") on the clay courts of [Lille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lille "Lille"). After comfortably defeating Tsonga in his first match, Čilić found himself in the same position he was in the [2016 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Davis_Cup_World_Group#Croatia_vs._Argentina "2016 Davis Cup World Group"), having to win his second rubber to guarantee Croatia the title. This time however, Čilić defeated his opponent, [Lucas Pouille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Pouille "Lucas Pouille"), in straight sets to grab the decisive victory for Croatia.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-49)
### 2019: 500th career win, fall from top 30
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: 2019: 500th career win, fall from top 30")]
Čilić started his year at [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 Australian Open – Men's singles"). In his third round match against Fernando Verdasco, Čilić saved two match points and came back from a two set deficit to advance to the fourth round. This was the seventh time in Čilić's career that he had won a match after being down two sets.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-50) In the fourth round, Čilić was upset by an in-form Roberto Bautista Agut.
Over his next three tournaments, Čilić only managed to win one match, while being eliminated early at [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Dubai_Tennis_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 Dubai Tennis Championships – Men's singles"), [Indian Wells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_BNP_Paribas_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 BNP Paribas Open – Men's singles"), and [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Miami_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 Miami Open – Men's singles"). As a result of his poor form in the early hard court season, Čilić fell from the world's top ten for the first time in over two years.
After another two winless tournaments to start the clay court season (at [Monte-Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Monte-Carlo_Masters_%E2%80%93_Singles "2019 Monte-Carlo Masters – Singles") and [Budapest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Hungarian_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2019 Hungarian Open – Singles")), Čilić finally broke his slump at the [Madrid Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Mutua_Madrid_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 Mutua Madrid Open – Men's singles") by winning three consecutive matches against [Martin Kližan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Kli%C5%BEan "Martin Kližan"), [Jan-Lennard Struff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan-Lennard_Struff "Jan-Lennard Struff"), & [Laslo Djere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laslo_Djere "Laslo Djere") on the way to the quarterfinals. However, he had to withdraw before his match against Djokovic due to food poisoning. By reaching the quarterfinals, Čilić became one of the few players on the Tour to reach the quarterfinal stage of all [nine Masters 1000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_Tour_Masters_1000 "ATP Tour Masters 1000") tournaments. Čilić lost his second round match at both [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Italian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 Italian Open – Men's singles") and the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 French Open – Men's singles"), to Jan-Lennard Struff and Grigor Dimitrov respectively.
Čilić failed to defend his [Queen's Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Queen's_Club_Championships_%E2%80%93_Singles "2019 Queen's Club Championships – Singles") title, leaving the Croat out of the top 15 for the first time in five years. This also marked the first time since August 2008 that Čilić had not reached a tournament final in over a year. Čilić lost in the second round of [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles") to [João Sousa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo%C3%A3o_Sousa "João Sousa") in straight sets.
In the North American summer hard-court season, Čilić competed in [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Citi_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 Citi Open – Men's singles"), [Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Rogers_Cup_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 Rogers Cup – Men's singles"), [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Western_&_Southern_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 Western & Southern Open – Men's singles"), and the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2019 US Open – Men's singles") in New York. Čilić fell from the world's top 20 after failing to match his previous year's performance at the first three events. At the US Open, Čilić reached the fourth round where he showed improvements to form during a four set loss against eventual champion Nadal.
On 17 October 2019, he reached his 500th career match win at the [2019 Kremlin Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Kremlin_Cup "2019 Kremlin Cup") in Moscow becoming the 10th active player in the list.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-51) Čilić ended the year ranked No. 39 in the ATP rankings. It marked the first time that he had failed to win a singles title since 2007.
### 2020–2021: Olympic silver medal, top 30
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: 2020–2021: Olympic silver medal, top 30")]
Čilić started the 2020 season at the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2020 Australian Open – Men's singles") where he beat [Corentin Moutet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corentin_Moutet "Corentin Moutet"), [Benoît Paire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beno%C3%AEt_Paire "Benoît Paire"), and [Roberto Bautista Agut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Bautista_Agut "Roberto Bautista Agut") before losing to [Milos Raonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milos_Raonic "Milos Raonic") in straight sets. At the [Open 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Open_13_Provence_%E2%80%93_Singles "2020 Open 13 Provence – Singles"), Čilić lost in the round of 16 to [Denis Shapovalov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Shapovalov "Denis Shapovalov"). He lost in the first rounds of the [Dubai Tennis Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Dubai_Tennis_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2020 Dubai Tennis Championships – Men's singles") and the [Cincinnati Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Western_&_Southern_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2020 Western & Southern Open – Men's singles") to Benoît Paire and Shapovalov respectively. At the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2020 US Open – Men's singles"), he beat [Denis Kudla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Kudla "Denis Kudla") and [Norbert Gombos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norbert_Gombos "Norbert Gombos") before losing to [Dominic Thiem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Thiem "Dominic Thiem") in four sets. He was once again defeated by Thiem in the first round of the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2020 French Open – Men's singles") in straight sets.
Čilić began the 2021 season at the [Murray River Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Murray_River_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2021 Murray River Open – Singles"), where he lost in the first round to [Jérémy Chardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%A9my_Chardy "Jérémy Chardy") despite having five match points in the third-set tiebreak.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-52) At the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2021 Australian Open – Men's singles"), he lost to 18th seed [Grigor Dimitrov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grigor_Dimitrov "Grigor Dimitrov") in the first round.
At the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2021 French Open – Men's singles"), he was defeated in the second round by [Roger Federer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer") in four sets.
In June, Čilić won the [Stuttgart Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Stuttgart_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2001 Stuttgart Open – Singles"), defeating third seed [Félix Auger-Aliassime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9lix_Auger-Aliassime "Félix Auger-Aliassime") in the final in straight sets to win his 19th singles title and first in three years.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-53) At [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2021 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles"), he reached third round where he was knocked out by [Daniil Medvedev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniil_Medvedev "Daniil Medvedev") after winning the first two sets.
In July, Čilić competed at the postponed [Tokyo Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "Tennis at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's singles") and reached the second round in singles where he lost to [Pablo Carreño Busta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pablo_Carre%C3%B1o_Busta "Pablo Carreño Busta"). In the [doubles tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_at_the_2020_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_doubles "Tennis at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's doubles"), he and [Ivan Dodig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Dodig "Ivan Dodig") reached the final,[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-54) where they lost to compatriots [Mate Pavić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mate_Pavi%C4%87 "Mate Pavić") and [Nikola Mektić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Mekti%C4%87 "Nikola Mektić").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-55) It was the third time in the [Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Tennis at the Summer Olympics") men's doubles' history that the same country won both gold and silver, and the first one since [1908](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_at_the_1908_Summer_Olympics "Tennis at the 1908 Summer Olympics").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-56)
At the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2021 US Open – Men's singles"), Čilić retired in the first round in the fifth set against [Philipp Kohlschreiber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philipp_Kohlschreiber "Philipp Kohlschreiber"). It was his first retirement in more than 800 matches on the tour and the first time he had failed to make it past the opening round at Flushing Meadows in 13 attempts.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-57)
Čilić then competed at the [Kremlin Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Kremlin_Cup_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2021 Kremlin Cup – Men's singles") as the sixth seed where he reached the final. He beat [Damir Dzumhur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damir_D%C5%BEumhur "Damir Džumhur") in three sets before defeating [Tommy Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Paul_\(tennis\) "Tommy Paul \(tennis\)") in straight sets. He once again won in straight sets against [Pedro Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Mart%C3%ADnez_\(tennis\) "Pedro Martínez \(tennis\)") in the quarterfinals and against [Ričardis Berankis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ri%C4%8Dardas_Berankis "Ričardas Berankis") in the semifinals. He lost to [Aslan Karatsev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aslan_Karatsev "Aslan Karatsev") in straight sets in the final.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-59)
The following week, Čilić won the [St. Petersburg Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_St._Petersburg_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2021 St. Petersburg Open – Singles"), defeating fifth seed [Taylor Fritz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Fritz "Taylor Fritz") in a three-sets final to win his 20th singles title.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-60) On the way to the title, he also defeated [Albert Ramos Viñolas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Ramos_Vi%C3%B1olas "Albert Ramos Viñolas"), [Karen Khachanov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karen_Khachanov "Karen Khachanov"), [Roberto Bautista Agut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Bautista_Agut "Roberto Bautista Agut") and [Botic van de Zandschulp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botic_van_de_Zandschulp "Botic van de Zandschulp"). With this title he became only the sixth active player in 2021 with [20 titles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_Tour_records#Titles_&_finals "ATP Tour records") after Federer, Nadal, Djokovic, Murray and del Potro. He also returned to the top 30 after to years to World No. 28 on 1 November 2021.
### 2022: French Open semifinal and top 15
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: 2022: French Open semifinal and top 15")]
At the [Adelaide International 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_International_1 "Adelaide International 1") tournament, Čilić recorded his 550th win and became one of only seven active players to have over 550 wins and 40th man overall in the [Open Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Era "Open Era").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-61)
Čilić then entered the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2022 Australian Open – Men's singles") as the 27th seed. He defeated [Emilio Gómez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilio_G%C3%B3mez_\(tennis\) "Emilio Gómez \(tennis\)") in the first round in straight sets, [Norbert Gombos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norbert_Gombos "Norbert Gombos") in the second round in four sets, and fifth seed [Andrey Rublev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrey_Rublev "Andrey Rublev") in the third round in four sets. He lost to ninth seed [Félix Auger-Aliassime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9lix_Auger-Aliassime "Félix Auger-Aliassime") in the fourth round in four sets.
At the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2022 French Open – Men's singles"), Čilić defeated [Attila Balazs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attila_Bal%C3%A1zs "Attila Balázs") in the first round,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-62) [Marton Fucsovics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marton_Fucsovics "Marton Fucsovics") in the second, [Gilles Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilles_Simon "Gilles Simon") in the third before taking out number 2 seed [Daniil Medvedev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniil_Medvedev "Daniil Medvedev") in straight sets in the round of 16.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-63) With this result, he secured his return into the top 20 in the rankings. He won against [Andrey Rublev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrey_Rublev "Andrey Rublev") in the quarterfinals in a long five sets match with a super tiebreak in the fifth — the first ever played on Court Philippe Chatrier — winning the last 9 points in a row and lasting 4 hours and 10 minutes to reach his first semifinal at this Major.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-64) He became only the 5th active player besides the [Big Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Four_\(tennis\) "Big Four \(tennis\)"), and the first Croatian player to reach the semifinals at all four majors. He then lost to [Casper Ruud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casper_Ruud "Casper Ruud") in the semifinals.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-65)
At the [Canadian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_National_Bank_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2022 National Bank Open – Men's singles") he recorded his 350th hard court win, becoming only the fifth active player, behind the Big Four, to achieve this milestone.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-66)
At the [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2022 US Open – Men's singles"), Čilić defeated [Dan Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Evans_\(tennis\) "Dan Evans \(tennis\)") in the third round.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-67) In the fourth round, he lost to eventual champion [Carlos Alcaraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Alcaraz "Carlos Alcaraz") in a five-set match lasting nearly four hours.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-68)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87_u_Vara%C5%BEdinu_%282024%29.jpg/250px-Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87_u_Vara%C5%BEdinu_%282024%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87_u_Vara%C5%BEdinu_\(2024\).jpg)Čilić at the [2024 Davis Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Davis_Cup "2024 Davis Cup") in [Varaždin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vara%C5%BEdin "Varaždin")
In October, Čilić reached the final of the [Tel Aviv Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Tel_Aviv_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2022 Tel Aviv Open – Singles"), where he lost in straight sets to No. 1 seed [Novak Djokovic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novak_Djokovic "Novak Djokovic"), who was playing his first official tournament since winning [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2022 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-69) As a result, he returned to the top 15 in the rankings at world No. 14 on 3 October 2022.
### 2023–25: Lowest ranked ATP titlist, back to Majors & top 100, top 5 win
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: 2023–25: Lowest ranked ATP titlist, back to Majors & top 100, top 5 win")]
In the first week of 2023, Čilić reached the quarterfinals in [Pune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Tata_Open_Maharashtra_%E2%80%93_Singles "2023 Tata Open Maharashtra – Singles"), but injured his knee during the tournament and pulled out before his match against eventual champion [Tallon Griekspoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallon_Griekspoor "Tallon Griekspoor"). He did not play in any further tournaments since his injury[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-70) and fell out of the top 100 until his return at the [Croatia Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Croatia_Open_Umag_%E2%80%93_Singles "2023 Croatia Open Umag – Singles") in Umag.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-71)
In 2024, after another long hiatus, Čilić returned to the ATP Tour at the [2024 Hong Kong Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_ATP_Hong_Kong_Tennis_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2024 ATP Hong Kong Tennis Open – Singles") using a protected ranking. He also competed at the [2024 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2024 Australian Open – Men's singles") using a protected ranking.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-72) Čilić then received a wildcard for the [Argentina Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Argentina_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2024 Argentina Open – Singles"). He also entered the [Monte-Carlo Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Monte-Carlo_Masters_%E2%80%93_Singles "2024 Monte-Carlo Masters – Singles") and the [Mutua Madrid Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Mutua_Madrid_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2024 Mutua Madrid Open – Men's singles") using a protected ranking, but withdrew before the tournaments began. In May 2024, he withdrew from the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2024 French Open – Men's singles") having undergone knee surgery.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-73) In August 2024, after a six-month hiatus, he returned to the [2024 Manacor Challenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Rafa_Nadal_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2024 Rafa Nadal Open – Singles") and defeated [Alberto Barroso Campos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alberto_Barroso_Campos "Alberto Barroso Campos") in the first round.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-74)
Ranked No. 777, Čilić reached the semifinals at the [2024 Hangzhou Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Hangzhou_Open_%E2%80%93_Singles "2024 Hangzhou Open – Singles") as a wildcard with wins over two Japanese players, eighth seed [Yoshihito Nishioka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoshihito_Nishioka "Yoshihito Nishioka")[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-75) and qualifier [Yasutaka Uchiyama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasutaka_Uchiyama "Yasutaka Uchiyama"), saving two match points against the latter.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-77) Next he defeated fourth seed [Brandon Nakashima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Nakashima "Brandon Nakashima") to reach his 37th final and first in two years since September 2022 in Tel Aviv.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-78) As a result, he became the second lowest-ranked finalist after [Raemon Sluiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raemon_Sluiter "Raemon Sluiter") in 2009 in ['s-Hertogenbosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Ordina_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2009 Ordina Open – Men's singles").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-79) With his win over sixth seed [Zhang Zhizhen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhang_Zhizhen "Zhang Zhizhen") in the final, Čilić clinched his 21st title and 16th on hardcourts, becoming the lowest ranked player to win a title since the current ATP ranking system's introduction in 1973. As a result, he returned to the top 250 in the singles rankings, raising more than 500 positions on 23 September 2024.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-83)
Ranked No. 187 at the [2025 Dubai Tennis Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Dubai_Tennis_Championships "2025 Dubai Tennis Championships"), Čilić reached the quarterfinals defeating top-10 player and sixth seed [Alex de Minaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_de_Minaur "Alex de Minaur") and another Australian [Alexei Popyrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexei_Popyrin "Alexei Popyrin"), and rose more than 45 positions up, returning to the top 150 in the singles rankings.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-85)
Čilić won his first Challenger title in 17 years and 10 months at the [2025 Girona Challenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Girona_Challenger "2025 Girona Challenger") (since Rijeka, Croatia in 2007) breaking [Andy Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Murray "Andy Murray")'s record for the longest gap in winning titles on the [ATP Challenger Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ATP_Challenger_Tour "ATP Challenger Tour").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-86)
Ranked No. 109, Čilić played in the [2025 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_French_Open "2025 French Open"), his first French Open appearance since 2022 and his first Grand Slam tournament since the 2024 Australian Open,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-87) having been given a place in the main draw as a lucky loser after losing in the last round of qualifying to [Lloyd Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Harris_\(tennis\) "Lloyd Harris \(tennis\)").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-88) This was the first time that Čilić had played in the qualifying competition of a major since the [2007 US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_US_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles_qualifying "2007 US Open – Men's singles qualifying"). He lost in the first round to [Flavio Cobolli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavio_Cobolli "Flavio Cobolli").
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87%2C_Swiss_Indoors_Basel_2025.jpg/250px-Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87%2C_Swiss_Indoors_Basel_2025.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87,_Swiss_Indoors_Basel_2025.jpg)Marin Čilić, Swiss Indoors Basel 2025
At the [Lexus Nottingham Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Nottingham_Open "2025 Nottingham Open") Čilić lifted another Challenger title after reaching his third final for the season and returned to the top 100 in the singles rankings on 23 June 2025.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-89) At 36 and eight months, Čilić became the oldest grass court champion in Challenger history.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-90) He received a direct main draw entry for the [2025 Wimbledon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Wimbledon_Championships "2025 Wimbledon Championships") following a four-year absence at the tournament and upset world No. 4 [Jack Draper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Draper "Jack Draper") in the second round.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-91) It was his first Top 5 win since knocking out then No. 2-ranked [Daniil Medvedev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniil_Medvedev "Daniil Medvedev") in the fourth round at the [2022 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_French_Open "2022 French Open").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-92)
Marin Cilic lost in the round of 16 at the 2025 Swiss Indoors against [Felix Auger-Aliassime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9lix_Auger-Aliassime "Félix Auger-Aliassime"), who was a finalist at the [Paris Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Masters "Paris Masters") 2025.
### 2026: 600th career win
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: 2026: 600th career win")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/%C4%8Cili%C4%87_Rosmalen.jpg/250px-%C4%8Cili%C4%87_Rosmalen.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%C4%8Cili%C4%87_Rosmalen.jpg)Čilić at the [2026 Libéma Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Lib%C3%A9ma_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2026 Libéma Open – Men's singles")
With his second round win over [Denis Shapovalov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Shapovalov "Denis Shapovalov") at the [2026 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Australian_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2026 Australian Open – Men's singles"), Čilić recorded his 599th victory in the ATP Tour, tied with compatriot [Goran Ivanišević](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goran_Ivani%C5%A1evi%C4%87 "Goran Ivanišević").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-93) He then lost in the third round to [Casper Ruud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casper_Ruud "Casper Ruud").
At the [Dallas Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Dallas_Open "2026 Dallas Open"), Čilić recorded his 600th career win, the first man born in 1988 or later to reach the milestone,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-94) and the second active player after Djokovic.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-96)
At the [Libéma Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Lib%C3%A9ma_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2026 Libéma Open – Men's singles"), he won against [Denis Shapovalov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Shapovalov "Denis Shapovalov") in the first and [Nuno Borges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuno_Borges_\(tennis\) "Nuno Borges \(tennis\)") in the second round respectively, but lost to [Daniil Medvedev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniil_Medvedev "Daniil Medvedev") in the quarterfinals.
At the [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2026 French Open – Men's singles"), he lost in the first round to [Moïse Kouamé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mo%C3%AFse_Kouam%C3%A9 "Moïse Kouamé") and at [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Wimbledon_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men's_singles "2026 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles") he suffered another first round exit to [Daniil Medvedev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniil_Medvedev "Daniil Medvedev").
## Clothing and equipment
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Clothing and equipment")]
As of 2018 Čilić plays with the Head YouTek Radical MidPlus with a custom drilled 16x19 string pattern, painted to look like the Head Graphene Touch Prestige Mid. For strings he uses a hybrid of Babolat VS Touch mains and Luxilon ALU Power crosses. He wore [Fila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fila_\(company\) "Fila \(company\)") apparel until the 2011 season, when he got a 5-year contract with [Li-Ning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li-Ning "Li-Ning"), switching back to Fila in 2016.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_%C4%8Cili%C4%87#cite_note-97) At the start of the 2020 season, Čilić started wearing [Head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_\(company\) "Head \(company\)") apparel.
